how: Record the value in °C, at rest.

why.text: No NASA HRP risk names body temperature. It is tracked because fever or a low temperature needs attention, and the closed spacecraft environment is a NASA hazard.
why.uncovered_reason: No HRP risk names body temperature; Hostile/Closed Environments is a NASA hazard, not a risk.

if_abnormal.now: Check the thermometer and that the crewmember is at rest.
if_abnormal.remeasure: Measure again after the crewmember has rested, with the same device.
if_abnormal.tell_ground: Add the readings to the next ground report.

space_note: Resting core temperature rose about 1 °C over 2.5 months of long-duration flight (Stahn 2017), so detection expects +1 °C. Safety bound 35 to 38 °C: below 35 °C is hypothermia (NASA-STD-3001); 38 °C is the CDC fever definition (Earth reference, no space data).
